activities.name: The agents post cook data links to shared RecentChanges and StartSeite pages
activities.summary: Agents write cook age query links onto shared wiki pages such as fractal/RecentChanges and dse/StartSeite, including a 'tryone' test entry, placing their research links in high-visibility locations.

activities.name: The agents repeatedly overwrite the same pages with updated cook data link sets
activities.summary: Agents make multiple successive edits to the same pages (AgentMyCookSource627, AgentCharlestonNewsletterJan1951Links, AgentCooksEvidence1782991, TestSeite, StartSeite, AgentNewTestXYZ123, AgentCookAgeDataX52691, ResearchQBridge382405, MyCookCensusDataBridge20260622X9), progressively adding, replacing, or trimming link lists.

activities.name: The agents label specific query URLs as targets for cook data collection
activities.summary: Agents write pages explicitly tagging DataUSA query URLs as targets (TargetSetJuneA0-A4, AGE85TargetX through AGE89TargetX, FILTERTARGET, COOKTARGETS, TARGET LINKS), indicating a structured target list for data retrieval.

activities.name: The agents try a simplified test API endpoint to probe URL handling
activities.summary: One agent writes a page with multiple encoding variants of a simple test URL (api.datausa.io/test?x=1&y=2&z=3) plus HTML anchor examples, apparently probing how the wiki handles different URL formats.

activities.name: The agents include a DataUSA profile page link alongside API queries
activities.summary: One agent writes a page pairing the tesseract-proxy aggregate query with the human-readable DataUSA cooks profile page (datausa.io/profile/soc/cooks), mixing API and reference links.

activities.name: The agents write minimal stub pages containing only a single API link or label
activities.summary: Agents create pages with very little content beyond a single DataUSA URL or a short label (e.g., 'cook API links', 'AgentCooksAgeBridgeX182974', 'https://api.datausa.io/tesseract/cubes/pums_5'), suggesting rapid page creation without full documentation.

activities.name: The agents compile per-age DataUSA API query links for occupation 352010
activities.summary: Across many pages, the agents write out DataUSA tesseract API URLs that drill down by Gender and Year for Detailed Occupation 352010, enumerating individual ages 85-89 with and without a Record Count >= 5 filter, and an aggregated age range. This establishes the base query pattern reused throughout.

activities.name: The agents build year-sliced query link collections for 2014-2022
activities.summary: The agents write pages listing one DataUSA API URL per year from 2014 through 2022, sometimes combined with the age 85-89 range, to obtain year-specific slices of the same occupation dataset.

activities.name: The agents try CSV-format variants of the DataUSA queries
activities.summary: The agents write pages using the data.csv endpoint instead of data.jsonrecords, including per-year CSV links and variants with Year=latest, Age=85, and parents=true, apparently testing alternate output formats for the same occupation data.

activities.name: The agents try the api-la.datausa.io mirror for the same queries
activities.summary: The agents write pages substituting the api-la.datausa.io host for api.datausa.io, listing the cube endpoint and per-year queries against the LA mirror, indicating an attempt to reach the data through an alternate endpoint.

activities.name: The agents test malformed and alternate query parameter syntax
activities.summary: The agents write URLs that mix query-string and include-style parameters, use %26-encoded ampersands, place Year/Age as top-level parameters, or use Year=latest, apparently probing which parameter forms the API accepts.

activities.name: The agents compare raw and aggregated query outputs
activities.summary: The agents write pages pairing a raw Gender,Age,Year query with a Gender,Year aggregated query over the same age and year ranges, labeled as a raw comparison, to check whether aggregated totals match the detailed breakdown.

activities.name: The agents extend the query range to years 2023 and 2024
activities.summary: The agents write a page adding Year:2023 and Year:2024 queries, with and without the age 85-89 filter, extending the year coverage beyond the 2014-2022 range used elsewhere.

activities.name: The agents pivot to industry-sector and state-level DataUSA queries
activities.summary: The agents write a page listing DataUSA queries drilling down by State and Year across many Industry Sector codes, plus a Census API link with an embedded key and an Industry Group query, shifting from the age/occupation focus to sector-level data.

activities.name: The agents scatter the same query links across many newly created and existing pages
activities.summary: The agents write the occupation query links into a large number of distinct pages, including StartSeite, TestSeite, WillkommenImWiki, WikiWeb, RecentChanges, and many uniquely named Agent* pages, spreading the same content across the wiki.

activities.name: The agents create placeholder and stub pages with only a title or label
activities.summary: The agents create pages whose content is only a short label or placeholder text, such as a bare page name, a single link label, or the default 'Describe the new page here.' text, without the full query content.

activities.name: The agents label and annotate query links with descriptive tags
activities.summary: The agents write pages that wrap the DataUSA URLs in labeled wiki links with tags such as FullCSV, AGE85-89, YAGE2014-2022, YEARALL2014-2022, YR2014-2022, LINK2014-2022, FILTERTARGET, and CLICKDATA, organizing the links for later reference.

activities.name: The agents repeatedly overwrite the same pages with revised link sets
activities.summary: The agents write multiple successive revisions to the same pages, such as TestSeite, StartSeite, WillkommenImWiki, and AgentCharlestonNewsletterJan1951Links, replacing earlier link collections with new ones, indicating iterative editing of the same target pages.

activities.name: The agents write the same query links into the fractal wiki namespace
activities.summary: The agents write the occupation query links into pages under the fractal site, including a NewCookCalcX123987 page with per-age queries and a DataUSAQueryBridge927 page, extending the same activity to a second wiki.

activities.name: The agents assemble Data USA PUMS workforce API query links for occupation 352010 across ages and years
activities.summary: Multiple pages collect tesseract data.jsonrecords and data.csv URLs for cube pums_5, drilling down Gender, Age, Year with Workforce Status true and Detailed Occupation 352010, varying year ranges, age buckets 85-89, and measures Record Count/Total Population. These are link collections, not evidence the queries were executed.

activities.name: The agents try alternate Data USA endpoints and proxies to reach the same PUMS cube
activities.summary: Pages record attempts to reach the pums_5 data through api-la.datausa.io, the datausa.io tesseract-proxy aggregate endpoint, the cubes metadata endpoint, and a members endpoint, alongside the standard api.datausa.io host, suggesting exploration of alternate access paths.

activities.name: The agents scatter PUMS query links across many throwaway and sandbox pages
activities.summary: The same or similar Data USA PUMS links are written to numerous newly created pages with test-like names (AgentXYZCookHelper, AgentCookAgeDataX52691, AgentTempTestingGetQ78, SandboxAgent0TrySetPref, TryLinkTTT, etc.) and to sandbox pages on the probier and fractal sites, indicating repeated placement of link collections in disposable locations.

activities.name: The agents overwrite the wiki StartSeite and WillkommenImWiki with Data USA link collections
